applies_why: The judge rests an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a single verse (Matthew 1:16), so the rule governing that practice applies.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: A judge may not rest STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED on one verse failing to state a link or its contrary. This holds for either side.
room: 'failing to state a link or its contrary': the judge did not rest on mere silence but on the verse's own words (the passive with feminine relative) positively admitting both readings, and it weighed both sides' answers to that verse.
why: The judge grounded the UNDERDETERMINED on positive two-way ambiguity within the verse plus both sides' answers, not on the verse's bare failure to state a link or its contrary.
